title: Shared specs
summary: A catalogue of spec parts that several apps share, and adding one to an app.
description: Apps that sync, sign in or draw alike can share the part of their spec that says how. The part is written once in a catalogue repository; each app gets a copy, recorded in its root item's imports (S39).

stories.want: to see the shared spec parts I could use, and add one to an app in a few taps
stories.soThat: each app gets the same decisions without copying files by hand

requirements.text: The app keeps a list of catalogues on the device: repositories whose spec is made of shared parts. One is added by name on the Shared specs screen, or from a repository's menu, and removed on the screen.

The Shared specs screen lists each catalogue's shared parts, its top-level folders whose index.json gives a permanent id, read at the newest commit of its default branch. Each shows its logo, name, id, summary and how many requirements, parts and values it has, and opens in the spec browser.

history.text: The Shared specs screen lists each catalogue's parts, its top-level folders with an index.json, read at the newest commit of its default branch. Each shows its title, summary and how many requirements, parts and values it has, and opens in the spec browser.
history.reason: Shared parts have an identity now: only folders with a permanent id are offered, and the list shows the logo, name and id.

requirements.text: A part can be added to a repository picked from yours or typed as owner/repo, or straight to the repository whose menu opened the screen.

Before anything is written, the app says what adding the part does. It refuses, saying why, when the repository already has its own part at that path, imports it from another catalogue, imports a part that overlaps it, uses one of the part's ids elsewhere, or has a root item it can't read. A repository that has this version already is told so.

Adding a part opens a pull request into the repository's default branch with one commit: the part's files copied byte for byte, each checked against the original's object id; the files of an earlier copy that the part no longer has removed; and the import recorded in the root item, keeping its order, values and waivers. Its description tells a coding agent what to do next.

In the spec browser, an imported part shows its logo, name and permanent id, says which catalogue and commit it came from, linking to it there, and lists the named values the repository sets differently and what it waives in that part.

history.text: In the spec browser, an imported part says which catalogue and commit it came from, linking to it there, and lists the named values the repository sets differently and what it waives in that part.
history.reason: Shared parts have a logo and a permanent id now, shown where the part is read.

requirements.text: An earlier copy of a part is found by the part's permanent id. When the part was renamed in its catalogue since, adding it again moves the copy to the new folder, removes the old one and moves the waivers of parts by path with it; ids stay as they are.

`spec-llms.txt` says what adopting a shared part takes in a product, so that a coding agent doesn't have to ask: cite the part's requirements; meet all of them, without asking and without proposing waivers (only what the import already waives is left out, and only a contradiction with the product's own spec is asked about); make constants follow its values with a test; deprecate what the product had specified itself in favour of the shared ids; link; check; and leave the product's words and structure alone. The description of an import's pull request points to it and sums it up.

history.text: `spec-llms.txt` says what adopting a shared part takes in a product, so that a coding agent doesn't have to ask: cite the part's requirements, meet them or ask whether to waive one, make constants follow its values with a test, deprecate what the product had specified itself in favour of the shared ids, link, check, and leave the product's words and structure alone. The description of an import's pull request points to it and sums it up.
history.reason: Agents asked whether to implement or waive each requirement the product didn't meet. A product takes a shared part to have all of it: meeting it isn't a question, and waivers are the person's decision, made beforehand.

requirements.text: An imported part shows its import. In the outline, its row says which catalogue it came from, when that commit was made, how many values the repository sets and how many entries it waives, and marks a newer version in the catalogue. On the part, a panel shows the catalogue and commit, whether the copy is as copied, the values set and entries waived with their reasons, and whether the catalogue has the part as copied, has changed or renamed it, or no longer has it. A newer version leads to the catalogue's spec comparison from the copied commit to its newest, and to adding the part again, which opens on that part even when its catalogue isn't in the list.
